extraction.name: IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval)
extraction.description: IFEval is an evaluation benchmark for large language models focusing on verifiable instructions (such as word count constraints or keyword inclusion) that can be verified using simple, interpretable, and deterministic programs. It consists of 25 verifiable instruction types and 541 prompts.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.citeAs: Zhou, J., Lu, T., Mishra, S., Brahma, S., Basu, S., Luan, Y., Zhou, D., & Hou, L. (2023). Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.07911.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Prompts were synthesized through a four-step process: (1) generating a set of base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended, (2) using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts, (3) applying few-shot prompting to rephrase prompts to enhance phrasing diversity, and (4) manually checking and editing the rephrased prompts one by one.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Synthesized base prompts paired with 25 categories of verifiable instructions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Illogical prompts were filtered out using few-shot prompting, followed by diversity rephrasing and manual review and editing of each prompt.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Evaluation of model responses was conducted using deterministic, rule-based verification functions. Two criteria are defined: strict accuracy (exact verification heuristic) and loose accuracy (evaluates compliance across eight transformations including stripping markdown font modifiers, removing introductory lines, and removing concluding lines).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors analyze false negatives in strict verification (e.g., markdown tags causing false mismatches) and note that while the loose verification criterion alleviates false negatives, it can introduce false positives (e.g., altering word counts by stripping introductory lines).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Deterministic Python verification scripts and transformation functions.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Future work outlines intentions to expand the benchmark with more verifiable instructions, align them closer to real-world applications, and support multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Accurate instruction following is critical for LLM safety and reliability; failure or misunderstanding of instructions can cause unintended outputs with severe consequences in critical domains such as healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically due to edge cases. Loose evaluation criteria may introduce false positives. The current suite is limited to 25 instruction types and text-only modalities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking the instruction-following capabilities of Large Language Models.
